note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: # owner, once: Docker Desktop (WSL 2 engine, integration for Ubuntu), WSL 2 with Ubuntu, VS Code with the WSL and Dev Containers extensions

wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "mkdir -p ~/src && rm -rf ~/src/orders-app && cp -r '$src/src/orders-app' ~/src/ && cd ~/src/orders-app && rm -rf src/*/bin src/*/obj tests/*/bin tests/*/obj && sed -i 's/\r$//' scripts/*.sh .githooks/* .devcontainer/*.sh && git init -q -b main && git config user.name 'Alex Demo' && git config user.email alex.demo@contoso.com && git add . && git commit -q -m 'chore: import orders-app'"
# owner, off camera warm-up: in VS Code (WSL window on ~/src/orders-app) run Dev Containers: Reopen in Container, wait for 'Dev container ready', then Reopen Folder in WSL

screens.name: reopen
steps: Open Ubuntu (WSL) and run: cd ~/src/orders-app; export PS1='$ '; code .
In the WSL window press F1 and run: Dev Containers: Reopen in Container
Wait for the build (second run, cached image); the postCreateCommand terminal prints 'Hooks: .githooks | fetch.prune=true pull.ff=only'
If the nuget volume is new, keep the line 'Taking ownership of /home/vscode/.nuget/packages' in frame
Capture when the last line reads 'Dev container ready: dotnet 10.0.4xx | Python 3.x | gh 2.x' and the remote indicator bottom left reads 'Dev Container: Contoso orders-app (.NET 10)'
mask: Windows / WSL user name in paths, the title bar and the terminal prompt
Accounts menu at the bottom of the activity bar
screens.note: Optional checks from demo.md: a commit 'added stuff' is rejected by the episode 1 hook, 'build(devcontainer): add .NET 10 dev container' passes; python3 tools/devcontainer_check.py prints OK.

screens.name: run
steps: New terminal in the container: dotnet test   -> 'Passed!  - Failed: 0, Passed: 15'
Run: dotnet run --project src/Contoso.Orders.Api   (listens on http://localhost:8080)
Open the Ports panel: 8080 with the label 'Orders API'
In the Windows browser open http://localhost:8080/healthz: 'os' Ubuntu 24.04 and 'inContainer': true
Second tab: http://localhost:8080/orders?page=5 with pageNumber 5 and 37 items (collapse 'items' in the JSON viewer)
mask: Windows / WSL user name in paths and prompt
browser profile picture and bookmarks bar

screens.name: extensions
steps: Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X) inside the container
Show the section 'DEV CONTAINER: CONTOSO ORDERS-APP (.NET 10) - INSTALLED': C# Dev Kit, C#, EditorConfig, GitHub Actions, Python, Pylance, autopep8
Type eslint in the search box: ESLint shows 'Install in Dev Container' (it is not installed)
Optional second capture: Docker Desktop > Volumes showing orders-app-nuget

screens.name: wsl
steps: Left: Windows Terminal, Ubuntu tab: pwd  -> /home/<user>/src/orders-app ; docker version --format '{{.Server.Os}}'  -> linux
Right: Docker Desktop > Settings > General with 'Use the WSL 2 based engine' ticked
Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources > WSL integration with Ubuntu on
Two captures side by side in the edit are fine
mask: WSL user name in the pwd output and prompt (export PS1='$ ')

teardown: # owner: in VS Code run Dev Containers: Reopen Folder in WSL before this teardown
docker ps -a -q --filter label=devcontainer.local_folder | ForEach-Object { docker rm -f $_ }
docker images --format '{{.Repository}}' | Where-Object { $_ -like 'vsc-orders-app-*' } | ForEach-Object { docker image rm -f $_ }
blocked: Docker Desktop is not installed on the recording laptop (and its licence terms for Momento Galatico must be confirmed); install Docker Desktop and WSL 2 with Ubuntu before recording.
